summary: The verifier grades every README key as an exact JSON integer against sealed per-rule fixtures whose expected values I recomputed by hand from manual RC-3 and the instruction's keep-today's-step rule. Each named rule has a fixture that isolates it and rejects a plausible wrong implementation. The signed fuel and mileage partitions are all covered, fixed-answer shortcuts are defeated by relabelling, and I found no false-rejection path for a contract-valid package.

files_read: tests/shipped/app/src/rentcharge/* and tests/shipped/app/tools/rentcharge_run.py (manifest SHA-256 identical to the environment/app copies that were read)

checks_performed: Recomputed every expected bill in families 01-11 by hand from RC-3: days per rule 2.3, miles per rule 2.4, allowance 150/day per rule 3.2, fuel per rule 3.3, tax as 8.25% of (time + mileage) rounded half-up, and total. Also recomputed file revenue and tax for every family 01-11. All matched.

Spot-recomputed about 25 bills from 12-generated and 13-limits (2W0, Z-7GD1, DO-PA4-113, -XUC3, AAAAAAAAAA, Z-9, B, L5, L9, L11, L12, L16, L17, L29, L31, L34, L39, L72, L78, L85, L115, L122, L123, L167, L188). All matched. Read 13-limits in full: its agreement section and bills up to L27 with Read, and bills L27-L199 plus the file totals with Grep -o, because the single line is 60 KB.

Traced compare(): it checks branch, revenue and tax, then each bill in order for all 8 BILL_KEYS with type(actual) is type(expected), so a float or bool fails, and extra keys are ignored (tests/test_outputs.py:196-210).

Traced relabel(): the week shift leaves every naive-datetime rental length unchanged, the shift range keeps times inside 2000-2099, ids stay within the rule 1.3 alphabet and length, the shuffle carries the bills with it, and revenue and tax are unchanged (tests/test_outputs.py:280-311).

Traced load() and SILENT: short and fuller inputs, whose figures the manual leaves to today's code, appear only in families 08-11, and every fixture is itself checked against rule 1.3 (tests/test_outputs.py:45,157-193).

Traced candidate execution: setpriv as uid 65534 with no_new_privs, python3 -I -S, the verifier's own driver (which inserts /app/src into sys.path), /app readable (test.sh:16) but sealed against writes, bytecode writes failing silently, and parsing of stdout plus exit code 0 only (tests/test_outputs.py:107-149).
Traced the reward channel in test.sh:20-27: reward is 1 only if pytest returns 0 and the driver on the documented path still matches the shipped copy byte for byte.

Traced the shipped package in environment/app/src to establish today's steps: days = ceil(length/1440), allowance 100/day with max(0, ...), fuel = (out - in) * rate, tax = floor(taxable_including_fuel * 825 / 10000).
Noted that SHIPPED_RUN / bill_run(shipped=True) is never called by any grading test (it is used only in the unreadability probe). This is dead code with no grading effect, so it is not a finding.

coverage_sweep.category: Map each required behavior to an assertion that fails if it is missing or reversed
coverage_sweep.reason: Each rule in the instruction's bug list and RC-3 maps to a test and fixture. Grace 2.3: G1-G6, where G3 at +59 min gives 3 days and G4 at +60 gives 4. Allowance 3.2: M3 has 250 miles over 2 days (0 at 150/day, 1500 at 100/day). Turnover 2.4: T1-T4, plus T5 with equal readings giving 0. Refuelling fee 3.3: F1-F4, including F3 at rate 0 giving 1500. Tax base 4.1: X1 gives 2393 vs 3341 if fuel were taxed. Half-up 1.2: R1 at 16.5 gives 17 (floor 16, half-even 16) and R5 at 99.99 gives 100 (floor 99). File totals 4.3 and order: 07 plus every compare call.

coverage_sweep.category: Check the full core result (values, membership, order), not just existence or shape
coverage_sweep.reason: compare() checks bill count, per-index id, days, miles and all four charges plus total, and file-level branch, revenue and tax, all with exact native-type equality. Order is checked by index, and the 07 file order (Z9, A-1, 0, MMMMMMMMMM) is unsorted. Relabel shuffles the order.

coverage_sweep.category: Each named domain rule has a case whose outcome changes when the rule is wrong
coverage_sweep.reason: All rule-isolating cases appear in dedicated families (see above). Rule 4.3 summing: taxing the file sum once gives 8663 vs 8664 in 01 RC3-0001. Rule 4.2 total: covered by every bill. The combination of rule 2.3 and rule 3.2 (allowance on grace-adjusted days) is covered by M4/M5: 7d+59 min gives allowance 1050, and 7d+60 min gives 1200.

Each wrong implementation below fails at least one fixture. Unchanged shipped code: fails G1, M3, T1, F1, X1 and R1. Applying 2.3 grace to rentals under a day: S1-S3 would give 0 days, expected 1. Giving short rentals a 100-mile allowance: L1 101 miles gives 40, expected 0. Clamping fuel to 0 when the car comes back fuller: E2/E3/C1 would give 0, expected -650/-16000/-1800. Adding the fee whenever fuel is not short: E1 gives 1500, expected 0. abs(in - out) for miles: T1. Adding 1,000,000 when in <= out: T5. round() half-even: R1. Taxing fuel, including negative fuel: X1 and E2. Sorting bills: 07. Ceil days for the allowance: M4. A fixed answer: defeated by relabelled, shuffled and time-shifted generated files.

coverage_sweep.category: Contract-valid alternatives (formatting, ordering, implementation) are accepted
coverage_sweep.reason: Output comes from the fixed verifier-owned driver via json.dump, and the test parses it as JSON and ignores extra keys. Equivalent days formulas (floor + (rem > 59), ceil((L-59)/1440), max(1, ...) for short rentals) all give the expected values. The 1440-minute boundary gives 1 day under either the >= or the > definition of a day rental. Stdlib-only code works under -I -S because the driver inserts /app/src itself. No valid alternative is rejected.

coverage_sweep.category: Documented restrictions and lifecycle (driver unchanged, figures left to today's code, no added clamps)
coverage_sweep.reason: The byte-for-byte driver requirement is enforced by DELIVERED_BYTES == shipped and by the cmp in test.sh. The keep-today's-step promise is graded for days under a day and for the fuel charge of a car that comes back as full or fuller, and SILENT confines those inputs to the families that grade them. Inputs the instruction leaves open are never graded, because within_limits rejects any fixture outside rule 1.3.

coverage_sweep.category: Initialization-to-first-event transition in a state machine
coverage_sweep.reason: Billing is a stateless per-agreement computation plus file sums. There is no state machine.

coverage_sweep.category: Signed derived quantities: legal sign partitions discriminated
coverage_sweep.reason: Fuel difference: short (F1-F4), equal (E1, X2), fuller (E2, E3, C1, C2), and fuller at rate 0 (E4). Odometer difference: positive, turnover (T1-T4, L123) and equal (T5). Total and revenue can be negative (E3 total -5175). Tax base is never negative, so the half-up direction is unambiguous.

coverage_sweep.category: Semantic content vs native encoding / representation / diagnostic output
coverage_sweep.reason: The verifier compares parsed JSON values and requires native int, which the README promises. It does not constrain whitespace, key order, extra keys or stderr, and it does not inspect package layout.

coverage_sweep.category: Stale binaries / self-controlled comparisons / unreachable cases
coverage_sweep.reason: Expected values are sealed, with ROSTER hashes and counts, and are independent of candidate output. The driver is replaced with the verifier's copy before any run. .pyc writes fail silently on the sealed /app, and Python revalidates .pyc files against source mtime and size. Every fixture passes within_limits, and the silent inputs are allowed only where they are graded, so no graded case is unreachable or out of contract.

interaction_sweep.case_or_path: M4 is 7d+59 min with 1051 miles: 7 days, 1 excess mile, 500. M5 is 7d+60 min with 1201 miles: 8 days, 1 excess mile, 1. Using ceil days for the allowance fails M4.

rules: days under a day kept from today's code
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: L1 is 5 h with 101 miles: 0. L3 is 1.5 h with 151 miles: 500. C1 is 45 min with 130 miles: 0. These reject both a 100-mile allowance and 0-day grace for short rentals.

rules: fuel charge kept from today's code for a car back fuller
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: E2 has fuel -650 with tax 825 on 10000, so fuel is excluded from the base, and total 10175. E3 has total -5175, which is summed into revenue 26650.
T3 goes 990000 to 10000 for 20000 miles over 5 days: 19250 excess miles times 30 = 577500. T4 does the same without turnover.
F3 is 1 eighth short at rate 0: 1500. E4 is fuller at rate 0: 0. Z-9 is 1 eighth short at rate 0 at the 2099 end: 1500.

rules: 4.3 file tax as a sum of per-bill taxes
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: RC3-0001 has six half-cent taxes that sum to 8664, while rounding the file base once gives 8663. R1 gives 17 under half-up, where half-even and floor both give 16.

Shifting both naive datetimes by whole weeks leaves every length unchanged, so the sealed bills stay valid. within_limits(run) is asserted on the relabelled file, and the shift bounds keep it inside 2000-2099.
